records.name: Thüringen
records.summary:
Thüringen's Landtag exhibits formal, multi-layered hostility to gender policy: an AfD fraction motion demands consistent implementation of a ban on gender-inclusive language in Thuringian schools, asserting schools must not be "a socio-political experimental field"; a draft law titled "Thüringer Gesetz zur Beendigung gleichstellungspolitischer Maßnahmen" proposes to dismantle the Land's existing equality-policy machinery, arguing that current law "regularly violates the principle of equal opportunity." Thüringen is also a partner in the Sachsen/Sachsen-Anhalt June 2026 Bundesrat initiative to tighten the federal SBGG. The dossier characterises the parliament as "formally hostile to gender policy."

National score is 0.71. Thüringen sits 0.06 below: the equality-dismantling bill is the most consequential institutional signal in this dossier for a visitor — if enacted, a trans person reporting an incident would find no Land-level equality apparatus. The gender-language motion compounds this at the administrative interface. Compared to Sachsen-Anhalt (0.68), Thüringen goes beyond tightening one federal law to actively removing the entire state equality framework; compared to Brandenburg (0.66), the threat is legislative and institutional rather than physical but arguably more pervasive for a visitor's access to recourse. records.name: Wales
records.summary:
Wales's devolved administration has publicly maintained its LGBTQ+ Action Plan through the UK's post-judgment years: the plan's standing update page was issued answering the For Women Scotland judgment of 19 December 2025, with a dedicated young-people's edition posted January 2026.

Its 'Rights, Respect, Equality' statutory school guidance (consultation May 2025) obliges schools to challenge bullying and harassment on the grounds of sex, gender reassignment and sexual orientation, with incident recording and monitoring and a parental escalation route. The practical facility rules set state-wide are unchanged here, but the visible institutional commitment — maintained action plan, statutory recording duties — is an official posture of inclusion at a national moment of rollback.

records.name: Northern Territory
records.summary:
The Anti-Discrimination Amendment Act 2025 (No. 27 of 2025, assented 30 October 2025; Part 3 in force 27 July 2026) removed the civil provision making it unlawful to "offend, insult, humiliate or intimidate" a person in public on the basis of a protected attribute, including gender identity. The NT is the only Australian jurisdiction that has actively reversed anti-discrimination protection rather than extended it; the government framed the rollback as "restoring freedom of speech and religion." For a visitor, public verbal abuse or humiliation directed at gender expression is now deliberately outside NT law while other states have brought it inside.

Federal protections continue to apply uniformly: the Sex Discrimination Act 1984 covers gender identity in every state and territory, and NT hate-crime penalty enhancements for SO/GI-motivated offences (2022 amendment, effective 2023) remain in force. No criminal expression ban, no facility-access ban, and no conversion-practice-specific enforcement issue arises for a short-term visitor beyond the general federal framework.
